DraftOdds.oprUp: Seed {seed} gives {basePct}%, but sitting in the event's {oprPct}th OPR percentile raises it: captains look at capability, not just the standings.
DraftOdds.oprDown: Seed {seed} gives {basePct}%, but an OPR in the {oprPct}th percentile lowers it — at equal seed, captains prefer the higher scorer.

note.insufficient: Not enough events yet to separate growth from volatility. With 3+ events this reading becomes reliable.
note.stable: Even performance event to event: what you show is what you are. To move up a tier you have to shift the average, not the variance.
note.growthLag: Your spread is growth, not inconsistency: the trend explains {r2Pct}% of it. The real problem is that your season OPR runs {scoutingGap} points behind your current form — and captains scout you on that lagging number.
note.growthClear: Clear growth trend (+{slope} OPR per event). The lever is holding the slope, not reducing variance.
note.decline: The trend is heading down ({slope} OPR per event). Before optimizing anything, find what degraded: mechanical wear, late design changes, or progressively stronger fields.
note.volatility: Your spread is noise, not trend: the line only explains {r2Pct}% of it, so every event is a coin flip between {min} and {max} OPR. The lever is raising the floor (failures, reliability), not the ceiling.
note.mixed: A mix of growth and noise: the trend explains {r2Pct}% of your spread and the rest is real volatility (±{residualSigma} OPR). Worth attacking both fronts.

SeasonAnalysis.title: Season Analysis
SeasonAnalysis.desc: The season read live from official results: how the team's output moved event to event, how much of that movement is a trend rather than noise, and what it means for alliance selection.
SeasonAnalysis.methodology: Per-event values are the team's average net points (score minus fouls) in qualification matches — the app's stand-in for OPR. It credits the whole alliance's output to the team, so it runs high compared with a least-squares OPR: read it as a within-team trend across this season, not as a figure comparable between teams.

strategy.topOrdered: Ordered field and you're up top: results tend to respect OPR. Ideal.
strategy.topChaotic: You're up top but the field is volatile: favorite with upset risk — lock in your seed during quals.
strategy.topTypical: Competitive position in a typical field: your quals seed decides your luck.
strategy.bubbleChaotic: Bubble zone in a chaotic field: upsets are common — a good day gets you into playoffs.
strategy.bubbleTypical: Bubble zone: you need an above-average event to make playoffs.
strategy.outChaoticUpside: Strong but volatile field: tough, though the chaos gives more openings than an ordered field.
strategy.outAboveLevel: Field above your current level: valuable as experience, unlikely for playoffs.

autoTeleopLevers.title: Auto raises the ceiling; teleop raises the floor
autoTeleopLevers.body: They're two different levers, not one. Auto is the weakest point by level (top {autoTopPct}% worldwide vs. top {teleopEndgameTopPct}% in teleop/endgame) and it's already growing steadily (+{autoSlope} OPR per event): that's where the most world rank is gained. Teleop is the opposite case — strong level but the season's most unstable phase (±{teleopNoise} OPR of noise the trend doesn't explain). There, the win isn't ceiling — it's consistency.

publicNumberLag.title: The public season number lags real form
publicNumberLag.body: The season OPR ({seasonOpr}) averages the early events and sits {gap} points below current form ({currentForm}). Since captains scout on that number, the gap costs draft position: the lever isn't reducing variance — it's making recent form visible.

nextTier.title: The next step is the veteran tier ({veteranFloor}+ OPR)
nextTier.body: Established Mexican programs run {veteranFloor}-{veteranCeiling} OPR. The elite benchmark is Devolt Phobos ({eliteTeamNumber}), world rank {eliteWorldRank} — a map of how far the program can grow.

rpAndSeed.title: RP bonuses and seed are worth gold
rpAndSeed.body: In double elimination, a top-4 seed is worth disproportionately more because of the byes. Being 'pickable' to top captains (consistent, visible auto) outweighed two ranking spots at FPEMX — the PRIDE model called {correct} of {total} playoffs correctly.
